title: Ambient-Air Fabrication of Methylammonium Lead Iodide Perovskite Solar Cells

paragraphs.text: We report ambient-air fabrication of methylammonium lead iodide perovskite solar cells with a certified initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under 1-sun AM1.5G illumination.
Perovskite photovoltaics have advanced rapidly, and ambient-air processing remains a key manufacturing challenge for the field.
The absorber layer is methylammonium lead iodide, deposited by spin coating from a DMF precursor solution in ambient air.
A compact TiO2 electron transport layer was prepared by spray pyrolysis of titanium diisopropoxide bis(acetylacetonate) at 450 C directly on the FTO substrate.
Current density-voltage curves were recorded with a source meter under a calibrated solar simulator at 1-sun.
The champion device reached a PCE of 21.1% at 1-sun illumination; hysteresis index was not reported in this study.
XRD patterns confirmed the tetragonal perovskite phase of the methylammonium lead iodide films.
Steady-state photoluminescence quenching indicates efficient electron extraction into the TiO2 layer.
We used UV-Vis spectroscopy to estimate an optical band gap of 1.55 eV for the absorber.
Devices were encapsulated with UV-curable epoxy before any stability testing.
L. Chen supervised the project and M. Ortiz performed the device fabrication.
Measurement files are deposited with the journal as supporting information.
